title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Chip Stocks Wipe Out as the Dow Floats
conditions.summary: AI spending worries and an oil spike sank tech, sending the Nasdaq down 2.6% and the S&P 500 down 1.2%. The Dow and small caps held flat as bonds rallied hard.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: S&P 500 fell 1.21% to 7,663.43; Nasdaq Composite fell 2.60% to 26,008.86, its worst day since June.
Dow edged up 0.02% to about 52,868; Russell 2000 rose 0.11% to 2,784.03.
AI spending and borrowing-cost worries hit chips and hyperscalers; the Nasdaq-100 fell 2.9%.
Oil jumped on reports of possible renewed strikes on Iran and an attack in Saudi Arabia; Brent closed near $113.
Consumer staples and utilities led; tech, industrials and materials lagged.
Breadth was negative on the Nasdaq, with 1,734 decliners against 1,471 advancers.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: Weekly jobless claims fell to 194,000, the lowest in three months and below forecasts.
The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 19 basis points to roughly 4.95%, back below 5% for the first time since Sept. 23; the 2-year fell about 14 basis points.
Fed officials are in their blackout period ahead of the Oct. 28 decision; markets price low odds of an October hike but high odds of one by December.
Gold fell about 2.6% as haven money flowed into Treasuries instead; the dollar index was flat near 101.6.
Bitcoin dropped about 4% to near $81,200, with roughly $400 million in crypto liquidations.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: MRNA (Moderna): -17.6% — reported leak of Phase 3 melanoma vaccine data that looked weaker than hoped.
LRCX (Lam Research): -11.8% — guidance only met forecasts and it flagged supply constraints.
CRWV (CoreWeave): -10.1% — worries about borrowing costs and its debt-heavy balance sheet.
SPCX (SpaceX): -9.1% — gave back much of Wednesday's post-earnings gain.
AMD (Advanced Micro Devices): -8.1% — caught in the AI chip selloff.
META (Meta Platforms): -7.0% — strong quarter overshadowed by AI spending concerns.
BX (Blackstone): +8.4% — upbeat outlook for fourth-quarter asset sales.
SPOT (Spotify): up more than 9% at midday — better margins and subscriber growth.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Tesla beat on adjusted EPS ($0.48 vs. $0.44) with revenue roughly in line, but fell 3.1%.
Lockheed Martin beat and raised its 2026 EPS guidance; Honeywell also raised guidance.
IBM beat but kept its revenue growth outlook and slid; Lam Research beat but fell nearly 12%.
After the close: Western Digital beat and guided above forecasts but dipped about 3%; Bloom Energy beat and raised its outlook but fell about 5%.
After the close: Deckers fell about 7% on soft guidance; Comfort Systems fell about 5% despite a beat; RingCentral jumped about 14%.

sections.title: Business News
items: LSEG agreed to buy credit data provider Octus for $3.535 billion in cash, expected to close in the first half of 2027.
Lockheed Martin secured a 10-year F-35 production framework agreement.
Eli Lilly broke ground on a $5 billion manufacturing plant in Goochland County, Virginia.
Cheniere agreed to a long-term LNG supply deal with QatarEnergy for 4 million tonnes a year.
France's 10-year yield rose above the US 10-year for the first time since 2013.

sections.title: On Deck
items: 8:45 AM CT: S&P Global flash manufacturing, services and composite PMIs for October.
9:00 AM CT: Final October University of Michigan consumer sentiment and inflation expectations.
Before the open: American Express, SLB, Autoliv and Booz Allen Hamilton report.
No Fed speakers scheduled during the pre-meeting blackout; the FOMC decision is Oct. 28.
Moderna's full melanoma vaccine data is due at ESMO on Oct. 24.

Now the lineup. Moderna dropped about seventeen and a half percent on leaked melanoma vaccine data. Space X slid about nine percent. Meta lost about seven percent as A I spending fears drowned out a strong quarter. On the bright side, Blackstone caught a clean wave, up more than eight percent on an upbeat outlook.
